title: Exact autoregressive sampling of planar Ising spin glasses via the Kac--Ward theory
authors: Jing Liu, Tao Chen, Tianrui Che, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Pan Zhang
abstract: Exact sampling from the Boltzmann distribution of spin glasses remains an outstanding challenge: Markov chain Monte Carlo methods suffer from critical slowing down and metastable trapping, while modern neural autoregressive samplers such as variational autoregressive networks are approximate and, in the absence of exact reference samples, cannot be rigorously benchmarked. Here we present an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm for planar Ising spin glasses based on the Kac--Ward theory. Under the chain-rule factorization, sequentially fixing spins induces boundary-localized external fields, which destroy the zero-field structure required for exact evaluation. By encoding these fields with a planarity-preserving auxiliary spin construction, the conditional partition functions are mapped to an extended zero-field Ising model and exactly evaluated using the Kac--Ward determinant formula. The method generates strictly independent and identically distributed samples with exact normalized likelihoods at a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(N^{5/2})$ for $N$ spins, thereby providing an exact baseline for benchmarking neural autoregressive samplers.
summary: This paper presents an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm for planar Ising spin glasses by creatively adapting the Kac--Ward theory. It overcomes the mathematical hurdles posed by boundary fields in conditional probability calculations using an auxiliary spin construction. The resulting method generates perfectly uncorrelated samples, offering a crucial, exact benchmark for validating approximate machine learning samplers in disordered systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving exact sampling from the Boltzmann distribution of spin glasses, as standard MCMC methods suffer from critical slowing down, and modern neural samplers are only approximate.
main_result: The authors developed an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm that generates strictly i.i.d. samples with exact normalized likelihoods, providing a rigorous baseline for benchmarking machine learning samplers.
method: The method adapts the Kac--Ward theory by introducing a planarity-preserving auxiliary spin construction to map the conditional partition functions, which are otherwise corrupted by boundary fields, into an extended zero-field Ising model solvable by a determinant formula.
model_or_system: The system studied is the planar Ising spin glass, governed by the Hamiltonian E(s) = -sum<i,j> J_ij s_i s_j. The analysis is applied to specific cases like the triangular AFM Ising model.
key_observables: Autocorrelation function (expected to be delta-correlated, $\delta_{t,0}$), Entropy (S), Magnetization (|m|), and Specific Heat (c_v).
important_parameters: Temperature (T), system size (N), and the coupling constants J_ij.
main_assumptions: The method relies critically on the planarity of the underlying graph structure and the successful construction of the auxiliary spin to maintain solvability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sampling process using auxiliary spins, compare autocorrelation functions (Metropolis vs. exact sampler), and show temperature dependence of observables like entropy and specific heat.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the difficulty of exact sampling, introduces the Kac--Ward theory framework, details the novel auxiliary spin construction to handle boundary fields, derives the conditional probabilities via determinant ratios, and finally validates the method by calculating observables like entropy and comparing autocorrelation functions.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the development of an exact, non-Markovian sampling technique that provides a rigorous benchmark for neural samplers is highly relevant to developing robust generative models for complex physical systems.

FIG. 2. Autocorrelation function Γ(t) of the energy for the 2D EA spin glass. The simulation was performed on a 16×16 lattice at temperature T = 0.5 (β = 2). The Metropolis al- gorithm (orange) shows a stretched exponential decay, while the exact autoregressive sampler (blue) yields Γ(t) = δt,0, con- firming strictly i.i.d. samples. The disorder realizations are taken from Ref. [24]. Data are averaged over 100 independent runs.

FIG. 3. Validation on the triangular FM Ising model. The magnetization per spin |m| (red, left axis) and the specific heat per spin cv (blue, right axis) are plotted as a function of temperature T. The values are estimated on 10 000 i.i.d. samples. The specific heat curve for L = 64 is obtained by directly differentiating ln Z with respect to temperature. The vertical dotted line indicates the theoretical critical tempera- ture Tc = 4J/ ln 3 ≈3.641.
